statements.status_notes: When an external mount.<type> helper ran but exited with an error, libmount still ran its privileged post-mount hooks (X-mount.idmap, X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, X-mount.mode), so a local user allowed an fstab mount could get root-privileged changes applied to the filesystem already under the target. Upstream fixed it in util-linux 2.41.6 (commit https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/a15c00a9e545aa8b9cf6ec0f888ff6c7b3eaeedc) and 2.42.3 (commit https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/1d14676ea70003e9f5b2a6a76af0cadb1190411a); see https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-m25x-3hj9-m26f and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-76642. Checked the libmount library in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 util-linux packages (2.41.2-r0, 2.41.4-r0, 2.41.6-r0 and 2.41.6-r1) on x86_64 and aarch64. These packages are built from the upstream release tarball for their version, with Alpine's packaging patches, and each libmount reports that upstream version. 2.41.2-r0 and 2.41.4-r0 (util-linux 2.41.2 and 2.41.4) are affected; 2.41.6-r0 and 2.41.6-r1 (util-linux 2.41.6) include the fix. The range ends at 2.41.6-r0.
